title: Chapter 3255 Quiet Before the Storm
content:
For once, the raging storm had quieted down, plunging NQSC into a ringing silence. At least that was what it felt like for the defenders of the city, who had been enduring the collapsing heavens for years — in truth, however, the city was far from quiet.

The roaring flames were consuming the blackened skeletons of towering buildings. The eerie wails of Nightmare Creatures rose in the distance, making the battered survivors feel like prey. The deafening thunderclaps of the storm were gone, but the darkening sky above the city still echoed with the booming cannonades of remaining turret batteries and artillery encampments. The lonely sounds of solitary rifles told the sorrowful tales of desperate last stands that happened here and there on the devastated streets of the ruined city.

"It's quiet."

On one such street, a young woman was carrying another on her back, both of them covered in soot and dried blood. She navigated the muddy rubble with tired steps, her eyes scanning the unrecognizable wreckage of charred buildings with wary alertness.

The ruins seemed layered here, rising in levels. Without the rain, one could enjoy quite a scenic view of what remained of NQSC — the districts that had already been flattened and flooded with abominations, as well as those that were still being defended by the stubborn human soldiers.

Nightmare Gates towered above the landscapes like black swords thrust into the body of the world.

“I don't like it.”

Rain's voice sounded uneasy.

She hesitated for a moment, then added in a subdued tone:

“Feels like the quiet that comes before the final storm."

A few moments later, Tamar's spoke weakly from her back:

"Why would you say that aloud, fool? Have you lost your mind? Ah, damn it... it's true what they say, the apple doesn't fall far from the tree."

In just a few days, it would be six years since the Lord of Shadows had departed to challenge the Nightmare. Humanity had endured for six long years, but now, it seemed like it was near the limits of its tenacity.

Half of the waking world — maybe more — had already been split apart and devoured by the Dream Realm. Antarctica, the Western Quadrant, and most of the Eastern Quadrant were already gone. The fate of America was unclear. Humanity had pulled back its forces to the Northern Quadrant and was defending it desperately, stubbornly clinging to every meter of ground.

If there was one silver lining to this apocalyptic calamity, it was that the three Supreme protectors of Earth could focus their efforts on defending a smaller area now — or it would have been, if not for the fact that the state of human strongholds in the Dream Realm was close to disastrous too.

Because of it, Soul Reaper Jet had joined the battle for the Dream Realm, leaving Earth in the hands of Nightingale and Raised by Wolves.

During the final death throes of the Western Quadrant, a Category Five Gate opened in its heart, unleashing Cursed Nightmare Creatures into the world. And when Africa was finally shattered and absorbed into the Dream Realm, those abominations were set loose in the hearts of both the Song Domain and the Sword Domain.

Now, another Category Five Gate was towering above the Eastern Quadrant, and the same catastrophe was bound to repeat itself in the coming months.

The Citadel Cities of the Dream Realm had been mostly cut off from each other, forcing humanity to establish several isolated, self-sufficient defensive frontlines. Much like the siege capitals of the waking world, several strongholds emerged as rugged cores of humanity's struggle to survive. Each of them supported several other cities, connected to them by Pathways of twisted space that Nightwalker had created.

In the northeast, the Sanctuary City of the Chained Isles had emerged as the linchpin of humanity's defenses. In the southwest, the city of Web that Ananke ruled and Misthaven ruled by Moonveil formed a twin bulwark that protected both the lower reaches of the River of Tears and the coastal waters of the Stormsea.

There were several smaller bulwarks of that kind scattered across the Dream Realm, as well as a few Citadel Cities that still managed to hold on despite being isolated from the rest of humanity almost entirely. Other cities had already been destroyed, diminishing the power of the human Domains and becoming mass graves for countless people who had sought shelter behind their walls.

And, of course, there were the two greatest strongholds of humanity — Bastion and Ravenheart.

At some point, they became one and the same.

For many years, Nightwalker had used the unique Component of his Great Citadel to prowl both worlds, assisting the faltering forces of mankind where his help was needed...

But with human territories in the waking world dwindling while the dreadful expanse of the Dream Realm became far too dangerous to move recklessly, he established his Dream Gate between Bastion and Ravenheart on a permanent basis, connecting the two great cities so that they could support each other and serve as the beating, indestructible heart of humanity in the dark days to come.

Even if all other Citadel Cities were destroyed, this impregnable stronghold would remain standing... it wouldn't fall until all humans were dead, and all human Supremes had been eradicated.

Great swarms of abominations. Cursed Nightmare Creatures crawling out of their ancient lairs to descend upon the human dwellings. Even the tides of profane power emanating from the dreadful darkness where the Unholy Ones stirred... by now, even the Supremes were struggling to stay alive on the battlefield, bearing dreadful wounds.

Saints, who had always been solitary champions, were now banding into cohorts to take on powerful Great Ones. More and more Transcendent powerhouses emerged from conquered Nightmares, but at the same time, more and more of them perished in the ruthless crucible of the apocalypse. The lives of Masters became cheap. Proud Awakened were reduced to mere footsoldiers...

But it was their resolve that kept humanity alive, and their sacrifice that bought Citadel Cities more time.

Rain had no energy to spare on pondering the fate of humanity, though. At the moment, she only worried about finding a shelter before the moon rose above NQSC.

"No, but isn't it ridiculous?"

Dragging Tamar through the ruins, she scoffed.

"You're a whole damn Saint. Why do I still have to carry you on my back? It's like nothing has changed since we were Awakened. Shouldn't you be carrying me instead?"

Her voice was carefree, but inside, she was fraught with tension. Tamar had been wounded quite gravely in the last battle — so, Rain kept talking to make sure that Tamar was still responding.

Any moment of silence filled her with dread.

Now, too, her friend was quiet for a few seconds. Then, finally, Tamar's hoarse voice resounded from behind, weaker than usual:

"It should be your honor to carry the young lady of Clan Sorrow on your back. You still have the gall to complain?"

Rain chuckled.

"Yes, yes... thank you for your generosity, Your Ladyship!"

Tamar moved slightly, tightening her grip on Rain's shoulders, then said in a somber tone:

"The moon will rise shortly. We need to hide ourselves underground, now."

Rain grimaced, looking around.

All around them were blackened ruins, the shapes of houses barely recognizable in the mess of collapsed, charred debris. Having been cut off from the rest of the garrison forces, they had already been lucky to stumble onto the stretch of the city free of abominations — finding a reliable shelter, though?

That seemed improbable.

She opened her mouth to retort, but stayed silent in the end.

Her expression changed subtly.

Sensing a slight change in her mood, Tamar asked:

“What?"

Rain remained silent for a moment, then let out a strange sound — half a laugh, half a gasp.

“No, nothing. It's just... I recognize this place."

The ruins were all but impossible to identify, but the unusual topography and the nearby landmarks were quite telling. She could not quite believe that it had taken her that long to realize.

Rain sighed, throwing another look at the charred rubble, and continued forward.

"I actually grew up here."

The collapsed piles of blackened debris had been neat houses once. The ashen mud under her feet had been green lawns and peaceful parks. It was the terrace district where her family home had once stood — so many years ago.

Now, nothing remained.

"Come on. I know a place where we can hide."
